chapter: Original Dixieland Jazz Band: Chicago and New York
title: Leaving New Orleans for Chicago and the Schiller Cafe; origin of 'jazz'
summary: The band travels to Chicago in March 1916, opens at the Schiller Cafe, and a patron's shout gives them the name jazz band.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Here we go. It's ready. We left New Orleans for Chicago Thursday, March 2, 1916, 8.30 a.m. I arrived in Chicago Friday, March 3, 1916, about 9.30. This train was late due to a severe snowstorm. Mom said, take you overboard. Mom don't know. We couldn't be bothered with those things besides it was warm in New Orleans. We did take our new straw hats and walk down Wabash Avenue in zero temperature with them. We opened at the Schiller Cafe owned by Sam Ahern, managed by Harry James, the latter style as a jazz band, J-A-S, and so advertised in that way. One night, as the Schiller patron became so emotional, he twirled a walking cane around his head and let it fly, hitting several people in his flight, shouting, jazz are up, fellas, jazz are up. We had never heard the term used before in connection with music or a band, and seen from that time on were known as a jazz band.
